# Plotting

## Exercise 8.1 {-}

For the countries Indonesia and Canada, create individual plots using
equirectangular, orthographic, and Lambert equal area projections,
while choosing projection parameters sensible for the area.

::: {.panel-tabset}
## R

```{r}
# +proj=eqc +lat_ts=0 +lat_0=0 +lon_0=0 +x_0=0 +y_0=0 +ellps=WGS84 +units=m
# +proj=ortho +lon_0=0 +lat_0=0
# +proj=laea +lon_0=0 +lat_0=0
library(sf)
library(tidyverse)
library(rnaturalearth)
ne = ne_countries(returnclass = "sf")
ne |> filter(admin == "Canada") -> ca
ne |> filter(admin == "Indonesia") -> ind
st_geometry(ca) |> st_centroid()
ca_eqc = st_crs("+proj=eqc +lat_ts=60.6")
st_geometry(ca) |> st_transform(ca_eqc) |> plot(axes=TRUE, graticule =TRUE)
ca_ortho = st_crs("+proj=ortho +lat_0=60.6 +lon_0=-96.4")
st_geometry(ca) |> st_transform(ca_ortho) |> plot(axes=TRUE, graticule=TRUE)
ca_laea = st_crs("+proj=laea +lat_0=60.6 +lon_0=-96.4")
st_geometry(ca) |> st_transform(ca_laea) |> plot(axes=TRUE, graticule=TRUE)
st_geometry(ind) |> st_centroid()
in_eqc = st_crs("+proj=eqc +lat_ts=-2.3")
st_geometry(ind) |> st_transform(in_eqc) |> plot(axes=TRUE, graticule =TRUE)
in_ortho = st_crs("+proj=ortho +lat_0=-2.3 +lon_0=117")
st_geometry(ind) |> st_transform(in_ortho) |> plot(axes=TRUE, graticule=TRUE)
in_laea = st_crs("+proj=laea +lat_0=-2.3 +lon_0=117")
st_geometry(ind) |> st_transform(in_laea) |> plot(axes=TRUE, graticule=TRUE)
```

## Python

```{python}
import geopandas as gpd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

ne = gpd.read_file("data/ne_ca_ind.gpkg")  # Natural Earth, as used by rnaturalearth
ca = ne[ne.admin == "Canada"]
ind = ne[ne.admin == "Indonesia"]

# country centres, as used for the projection parameters below
print(ca.geometry.union_all().centroid)
print(ind.geometry.union_all().centroid)

crs = {
    "Canada": {
        "eqc": "+proj=eqc +lat_ts=60.6",
        "ortho": "+proj=ortho +lat_0=60.6 +lon_0=-96.4",
        "laea": "+proj=laea +lat_0=60.6 +lon_0=-96.4",
    },
    "Indonesia": {
        "eqc": "+proj=eqc +lat_ts=-2.3",
        "ortho": "+proj=ortho +lat_0=-2.3 +lon_0=117",
        "laea": "+proj=laea +lat_0=-2.3 +lon_0=117",
    },
}
for name, g in [("Canada", ca), ("Indonesia", ind)]:
    for proj, p4 in crs[name].items():
        ax = g.to_crs(p4).plot(edgecolor="black", facecolor="none")
        ax.grid(True)
        ax.set_title(f"{name}: {proj}")
        plt.show()
```
:::

## Exercise 8.2 {-}

Recreate the plot in [Figure
8.3](https://r-spatial.org/book/08-Plotting.html#fig-figreset)
with **ggplot2** and with **tmap**.

**ggplot2**:

::: {.panel-tabset}
## R

```{r}
library(sf)
nc <- read_sf(system.file("gpkg/nc.gpkg", package = "sf"))
b = st_buffer(nc[1,1], units::set_units(10, km)) |> st_cast("LINESTRING")
library(ggplot2)
ggplot() + geom_sf(data = nc, aes(fill = BIR74)) +
		geom_sf(data = b, mapping = aes(colour = 'red')) +
		scale_fill_gradientn(colours = sf.colors())
```

## Python

```{python}
import geopandas as gpd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from plotnine import ggplot, aes, geom_map, scale_fill_cmap, theme_minimal

nc = gpd.read_file("data/nc/nc.shp")
# 10 km buffer around the first county: buffer in an azimuthal equidistant projection
first = nc.iloc[[0]]
c = first.geometry.union_all().centroid
aeqd = f"+proj=aeqd +lat_0={c.y} +lon_0={c.x}"
b = gpd.GeoDataFrame(geometry=first.to_crs(aeqd).buffer(10000).to_crs(nc.crs).boundary)

(
    ggplot()
    + geom_map(nc, aes(fill="BIR74"))
    + geom_map(b, color="red", fill=None)
    + scale_fill_cmap(cmap_name="Blues")
    + theme_minimal()
).show()
```
:::

**tmap**: see <https://r-tmap.github.io/tmap-book/>

::: {.panel-tabset}
## R

```{r}
library(tmap)
b = st_buffer(nc[1,1], units::set_units(10, km)) |> st_cast("LINESTRING")
tm_shape(nc) + 
	tm_polygons("BIR74", title = "BIR74") + 
	tm_layout(legend.outside=TRUE) +
	tm_shape(b) +
	tm_lines(legend.lwd.show = FALSE, col = 'red')
```

## Python

```{python}
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
nc.plot(ax=ax, column="BIR74", cmap="Blues", legend=True,
        legend_kwds={"label": "BIR74", "location": "right"})
b.plot(ax=ax, color="red")
ax.set_axis_off()
plt.show()
```
:::

## Exercise 8.3 {-}

Recreate the plot in [Figure
8.7](https://r-spatial.org/book/08-Plotting.html#fig-tmapstars)
using the `viridis` colour ramp.

::: {.panel-tabset}
## R

```{r}
library(stars)
library(viridis)
r <- read_stars(system.file("tif/L7_ETMs.tif", package = "stars"))
tm_shape(r) + tm_raster(palette = viridis(100))
```

## Python

```{python}
import rioxarray

# L7_ETMs.tif, copied from the stars R package into data/
r = rioxarray.open_rasterio("data/L7_ETMs.tif")
r.plot(col="band", col_wrap=3, cmap="viridis")
plt.show()
```
:::

## Exercise 8.4 {-}

View the interactive plot in [Figure
8.7](https://r-spatial.org/book/08-Plotting.html#fig-tmapstars)
using the "view" (interactive) mode of `tmap`, and explore which
interactions are possible;

::: {.panel-tabset}
## R

```{r}
library(stars)
library(viridis)
r <- read_stars(system.file("tif/L7_ETMs.tif", package = "stars"))
tmap_mode("view")
tm_shape(r) + tm_raster(palette = viridis(100))
```

## Python

```{python}
import folium
import numpy as np
from matplotlib import colormaps

# warp to lon/lat, as the web map needs
rw = r.rio.reproject("EPSG:4326")
rw = rw.where(rw != rw.rio.nodata)
xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax = rw.rio.bounds()

def band_overlay(b, alpha=1.0):
    v = rw.sel(band=b).values
    v = (v - np.nanmin(v)) / (np.nanmax(v) - np.nanmin(v))
    rgba = colormaps["viridis"](v)
    rgba[np.isnan(v), 3] = 0  # transparent outside the image
    return folium.raster_layers.ImageOverlay(
        rgba, bounds=[[ymin, xmin], [ymax, xmax]], opacity=alpha,
        name=f"band {b}")

m = folium.Map(location=[(ymin + ymax) / 2, (xmin + xmax) / 2], zoom_start=11)
band_overlay(1).add_to(m)
m
```
:::

Interactions: zoom, pan, linked cursor.

Also explore adding `+ tm_facets(as.layers=TRUE)` and try switching
layers on and off.

::: {.panel-tabset}
## R

```{r}
tmap_mode("view")
tm_shape(r) + tm_raster(palette = viridis(100)) + 
		tm_facets(as.layers=TRUE)
```

## Python

```{python}
m = folium.Map(location=[(ymin + ymax) / 2, (xmin + xmax) / 2], zoom_start=11)
for b in rw.band.values:
    band_overlay(b).add_to(m)
folium.LayerControl().add_to(m)  # switch layers on and off
m
```
:::

Layer switch on left-hand side (layer symbol).

Try also setting a transparency value to 0.5.

::: {.panel-tabset}
## R

```{r}
tmap_mode("view")
tm_shape(r) + tm_raster(palette = viridis(100), alpha = .5) + 
		tm_facets(as.layers=TRUE)
```

## Python

```{python}
m = folium.Map(location=[(ymin + ymax) / 2, (xmin + xmax) / 2], zoom_start=11)
for b in rw.band.values:
    band_overlay(b, alpha=0.5).add_to(m)
folium.LayerControl().add_to(m)
m
```
:::

This shows the base map shining through transparent raster colors 
(switch 3 of the 4 layers off to see this).
